subject: Isolation runway & commitment ladder: sizing proposal for CareWorks
messages:
From: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@careworks.health>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CareWorks compliance pilot — isolation sizing ask

Hi Stephanie,

Quick context — CareWorks is evaluating Redwood for a PHI-handling AI feature (chat + summarization of patient notes). Security team wants an isolated/private deployment option (VPC or air-gapped). Procurement & engineering asked for two concrete items so we can budget and draft the SOW:

1) A sizing band for an initial pilot (target: ~50k daily inference requests, peak concurrency ~220 requests/min, median prompt ~350 tokens) plus a 6–12 month runway to scale to 200k daily requests.
2) A commitment ladder/ops model: how to start with a smaller footprint (pilot) and grow without major rework — expected commit tiers, burst options, and fallback (e.g., hosted vs reserved).

Can you share a one-pager and a rough cost/latency expectation for Private vs Reserved (Dedicated) deployments and suggested MPA (milestones) we can insert into our procurement timeline? We need to present to our CTO and procurement by next Thurs.

Thanks,
Alice
Alice Jenkins
Director, Product — CareWorks Health

-----
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@careworks.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CareWorks compliance pilot — isolation sizing ask

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. I attached a short one-pager (redwood_private_vs_dedicated_onepager.pdf) and a sizing workbook (isolation_runway_calc.xlsx). High-level bullets below so you have something for the CTO deck immediately.

Two recommended starting lanes (both preserve PHI isolation):

- Option A — Dedicated (Reserved GPU pool):
  - Rationale: fastest time-to-value, predictable throughput, Redwood-managed runtime in a tenant-isolated environment (shared control plane).
  - Suggested initial commit: 4 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (we map to our slot model in the spreadsheet).
  - Expected p95 latency (chat): ~220–350 ms token latency under steady-state; burst capacity available via short-term add-ons.
  - Scaling ladder: 4 -> 8 -> 16 nodes; each step is a 3–6 week provisioning and capacity verification window.
  - Ops model: Redwood handles runtime updates, patching, and monitoring; customer network/VPC config required for egress controls.

- Option B — Private (VPC or on-prem private control plane):
  - Rationale: maximum isolation and compliance control, customer-managed control plane optionally with on-prem hardware.
  - Suggested initial footprint: 6 x A100-80GB or 4 x H100-equivalent (depending on model choice).
  - Expected latency: similar to Dedicated once tuned; slightly higher provisioning lead time and joint-runbook setup.
  - Scaling ladder: pilot (6) -> pilot+burst (10) -> committed fleet (20); typical onboarding 6–10 weeks for VPC control plane + security review.
  - Ops model: shared responsibilities — Redwood provides runtime + images; customer handles network, KMS/HSM integration if requested.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- Week 0: Sign pilot SOW (6-month term), SOC2 + SC attestations requested.
- Week 1–2: Technical kickoff + security intake (inventory + KMS plan).
- Week 3–6: Provision pilot footprint and run baseline benchmarks.
- Week 7–12: Canary with 10% production traffic, iterate on batching/quantization guidance (we'll provide per-model profiles).
- Month 3: Review metrics, agree to next ladder step (scale to target commit).

I'll loop in Marissa (SE) and Rishi (inference) for the sizing details and ops-runbook items. If this looks good I can turn the spreadsheet into a short appendix you can share with procurement.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CareWorks compliance pilot — isolation sizing ask

Hi Alice — quick technical color to help you evaluate the two lanes. I dropped a draft SLA exceptions doc (SLA_Exception_Draft.pdf) for the procurement team to consider when they need private-deployment carve-outs.

Sizing assumptions I used (also in spreadsheet):
- Model baseline: open LLM ~13B (typical for chat + summarization) — if you opt for a larger model, multiply the core counts accordingly.
- Typical request: 350 tokens in, 250 tokens out (on average) -> ~600 tokens total processing.
- Token throughput: on an A100-like node, optimized runtime, continuous batching -> ~70–140 reqs/min per node depending on batching window.

Recommendation for your concurrency: target 8 nodes for the initial private footprint if you plan to run heavier models or increase prompt length. For dedicated/reserved we can start at 4 nodes with aggressive batching and tuning; that reduces cost but increases SLO risk during unexpected spikes.

Quantization + ops notes:
- We strongly recommend mixed precision + 4-bit quantization profiles for lower-cost inference on non-critical models.
- For PHI-sensitive flows, prefer deterministic kernels and pin model versions; we'll provide a per-route tracing hook so you can audit inference paths.

Fallback pattern:
- Canary to Hosted / Lower-tier model variant if private cluster runs out of capacity (we include an automated routing policy).

[Attachment: sla_exception_draft.pdf (PDF)]

Happy to walk through the workbook with your infra team next week.

—Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Thanks — this is helpful. A few procurement questions before we escalate to legal: 
1) Can you provide a price range for the pilot and the next ladder step (numbers we can put in a budget line item)?
2) Can the pilot be structured with a termination window (we prefer 30 days after delivery milestones if the product doesn’t meet expected latency/throughput) and a 60-day notice for moving from pilot -> committed reserve?
3) We will need the SLA exception doc to include an audit timeline for logs retention and access for our auditors.

Also looping Naomi from our legal ops (CC'd) — Naomi, could you confirm which compliance artifacts you want upfront?

Best,
Ben
Director, Procurement — CareWorks Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Kline <ben.kline@careworks.health>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2026 15:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CareWorks compliance pilot — isolation sizing ask

Ben / Alice — thanks for the procurement questions. Proposed working answers so we can move to legal: 

1) Pricing ranges (pilot -> ladder):
  - Pilot (6-node private footprint, mixed 13B models): ~$45k–65k/month (infrastructure + managed runtime + monitoring).
  - Next step (scale to 12 nodes): additional ~$40k–55k/month incremental.
  - Dedicated reserved lane starting point (4-node reserved): ~$30k–45k/month; predictable but less headroom for burst.
  - Exact figures depend on final model choice, quantization level, and data egress requirements — workbook has line-item assumptions.

2) Contract mechanics:
  - We can do a 6-month pilot SOW with a 30-day exit window after the initial provisioning/acceptance milestones (we'll define acceptance tests in the MPA).
  - Transition to committed reserved capacity requires 60-day notice; we can define pro-rated credit if you convert during the pilot.

3) Compliance artifacts:
  - We'll share SOC2 Type II report and our redaction/retention playbook. For private deployments we support customer KMS and will provide audit logs with a 90–365 day retention window (configurable). The SLA exception doc will include log access SLAs and an audit-runbook.

Next steps I propose:
- Stephanie: send the updated MPA + pilot SOW draft (I can seed legal comments).
- Marissa / Rishi: schedule a 60-minute call with CareWorks infra for bench runs next Wed or Thu.
- Stephanie: include a DocuSign link for the pilot SOW so procurement can get internal approvals quickly.

DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.redwood/pilot/CW-2026-1092
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood/deal/CW-2026-1092
